rationale: C07 provides a concrete structural template for moving a distinguished officeholder from an existing position into a specially designated European diplomatic mission. Both letters acknowledge the recipient's current responsibilities, explain why prior experience uniquely qualifies him for the new assignment, frame the European mission as exceptionally important, and present ambassadorial service as the preferable continuation of his public career. C13 and C25 share narrower assignment-and-qualification patterns but lack C07's close transition-of-office and special-representative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If that is your preference, I earnestly hope that you will be willing to act for this nation with reference to the development of the North Atlantic Community
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In designating you to assume a post of great responsibility in the administration of the European Recovery Program, I realized that I was asking you to undertake a mission
shared_material.explanation: Both frame a new, demanding European assignment as a major national mission.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to act as my Personal Representative and Special Ambassador in the development of this new evolutionary step within the North Atlantic Community
shared_material.parent_excerpt: exceptional qualifications as United States Special Representative in Europe with the rank of Ambassador
shared_material.explanation: The offices are closely parallel: a presidential or United States special representative in Europe holding ambassadorial status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In case you do feel impelled to lay down the responsibilities of your present office, I can think of no way where you could better serve our nation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Under other conditions I would prefer to see you carry forward the work of the Department of Commerce... But that experience also adds to the equipment which gives you such exceptional qualifications
shared_material.explanation: Both letters connect departure from a current high office to a new assignment for which the recipient's accumulated experience provides exceptional qualifications.
